SECANT PILING

Secant Piles or Diaphragm Walls? Build the Comparison Around the Site

A practical framework for discussing two retaining-wall options without assuming a universal winner.

In this insight

Define the decisionCompare the construction footprintEvaluate cost across the sequenceMake the choice reviewableFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Define the decision

Secant pile walls are assembled from overlapping piles; diaphragm walls are formed in panels. Either may enter an early discussion about a constrained excavation. The selection is not a branding contest between methods. It is a project decision involving ground conditions, water, geometry, construction access and the intended role of the completed wall. Ask the design team to state the performance requirements before requesting alternative prices.

Compare the construction footprint

Look beyond the line shown on the basement plan. Equipment, reinforcement handling, concrete delivery, spoil removal and supporting operations all require space. An option that appears efficient in section may create a difficult site layout. Request a concept logistics plan for each option, including entry, material movements and interfaces with neighbouring works. Confirm which assumptions depend on permission to occupy land outside the boundary.

Evaluate cost across the sequence

Compare the total delivered package rather than a single unit. The evaluation should cover enabling work, wall construction, lateral support, excavation interfaces, water management, records and any permanent-wall requirements. Ask whether proposed savings create additional downstream work. Differences in risk allocation can also explain different prices: a quotation with broad exclusions is not equivalent to one with a defined responsibility schedule.

Make the choice reviewable

Record why the selected option suits the site, which alternatives were considered and what might trigger reconsideration. Keep that record with the design brief rather than burying it in an email thread. Where important ground or access information is missing, describe the selection as provisional. A clear decision record helps the procurement team resist late substitutions that change the engineering or delivery assumptions without proper review.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Set performance requirements first.
  • Compare site layouts and whole-package costs.
  • Record the conditions behind the preferred option.
